title: Wide-swing cascode mirror
description: The low-voltage cascode mirror. It keeps the matched-$V_{DS}$ accuracy of a cascode mirror but recovers the output swing a standard cascode wastes. The trick is the cascode gate bias: instead of the two-diode stack (which parks the mirror node a full $V_{GS}$ above ground), an explicit bias $V_{bias} = V_{GS,casc} + V_{dsat,mirror}$ places the mirror node at exactly one saturation voltage. The output then only has to clear two stacked saturation voltages, $V_{out}(min) = V_{dsat,mirror} + V_{dsat,casc}$, with no threshold overhead, so the output can swing far lower than a standard cascode's $V_{GS} + V_{dsat}$ floor. The two mirror devices still sit at the same low drain voltage, so the systematic error stays near zero. Both mirror devices bind width-first (output width = K times the reference); the cascode is modelled by one representative device (the matched reference and output cascodes share an inversion level). $V_{bias}$ is author math, and a rule checks it is realizable under the supply.

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves; the wide-swing floor lets this go low

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: mirror inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens matching but raises the saturation voltage the node sits at; the default keeps the compliance floor under the V_out default even on a high-V* device

params.name: vds_lo
params.note: the wide-swing mirror node. Solved, not retuned — the engine iterates it to the mirror device's own reported vdsat plus node_margin (the bias a real wide-swing generator is designed to produce), so the stored value is only a starting guess

params.name: node_margin
params.note: how far above the mirror devices' saturation knee the wide-swing bias parks the node — the customary 50-100 mV that keeps the mirror out of triode across corners

doc.title: Reference mirror device (bottom)
doc.description: The bottom reference device at the input current, biased at the wide-swing low node. Its saturation voltage sets where that node should sit, and the output mirror device shares the same vds.

doc.title: Cascode device (representative)
doc.description: One cascode device carrying the reference current; the matched reference-branch and output-branch cascodes share this inversion level. Its vgs sets the cascode gate bias and its saturation voltage sets the second term of the output compliance floor.

params.name: vds_cc
params.note: a representative cascode vds (its vgs and vdsat are the values used, and both are drain-voltage independent here)

params.name: vsb_cc
params.note: the source stands on the wide-swing mirror node, not the bulk

rows.name: wideswing_node
rows.note: where the wide-swing bias parks the mirror node: the saturation knee plus the design margin. vds_lo is solved to this

rows.name: sys_err
rows.note: lambda mismatch between the two mirror devices; near zero because both sit at the same wide-swing node voltage

rows.name: V_bias
rows.note: wide-swing cascode gate bias: one cascode vgs above the mirror node where the design actually parks it. That node is vds_lo — the saturation knee plus node_margin, which is what the solve produces — so biasing to the bare knee instead would sit the node a full node_margin low

rows.name: sigma_ratio
rows.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output resistance of the OUTPUT branch. The mirror device's own r_o sits in the cascode's source, so local series feedback multiplies the cascode's r_o by (1 + (g_m + g_mb)*r_o) and that degenerating resistance adds back in series; both source-referred generators feed back through it, so gmb belongs inside the factor — the same form the source-degenerated mirror uses with a resistor in that role. The K factors are what make this the OUTPUT leg rather than the reference one: casc is a representative device carried at the reference current, and the leg described here runs K times that through a K-times-wider device. At a fixed gm/ID, K times the current is exactly K times the transconductance and exactly K times the output conductance, so the scaling is an identity of the sizing rather than an approximation, and no separate output-branch device has to be sized to state it. This is the number a stage loading the mirror sees

rules.note: wide-swing output floor: the mirror node plus the cascode's own saturation voltage, with no threshold overhead (contrast vgs + vdsat for a standard cascode). The floor is measured from where the node is actually parked, vds_lo, not from the bare saturation knee — the node_margin that keeps the mirror out of triode across corners is headroom the output has to clear too
the cascode gate bias must be a voltage the supply can produce
